key_insight: Retinal OCT finding recognition does not ensure accurate localization: RetGrounder improved grounding F1 from 23.7% to 33.9%, but performance remained limited.
clinical_relevance: Localizing reported retinal abnormalities is important for assessing whether AI image interpretations are grounded in visible evidence.
method: Created RetinaGroundBench with ophthalmologist-annotated retinal OCT scans.
Introduced AggIoU to evaluate combined coverage from overlapping predicted boxes.
Evaluated 27 open-source MLLMs and fine-tuned the 8B RetGrounder using OCT grounding and textual information.
evidence_signal: The benchmark contains 815 B-scans and 4,537 bounding boxes spanning 13 biomarkers across 8 diseases; RetGrounder achieved a 43% relative grounding F1 improvement over the best general-purpose model.
watch_item: Grounding performance remains limited, and these benchmark results do not establish safety or effectiveness in clinical practice.
paper_title: A Visual Grounding Benchmark for Retinal OCT with Multimodal Large Language Models
